parameters.name: Enable
parameters.description: Enables or disables the interface. This parameter is based on ''ifAdminStatus'' from {{bibref|RFC2863}}.

parameters.name: Status
parameters.description: The current operational state of the interface (see {{bibref|TR-181i2|Section 4.2.2}}). {{enum}} When {{param|Enable}} is {{false}} then {{param}} SHOULD normally be {{enum|Down}} (or {{enum|NotPresent}} or {{enum|Error}} if there is a fault condition on the interface). When {{param|Enable}} is changed to {{true}} then {{param}} SHOULD change to {{enum|Up}} if and only if the interface is able to transmit and receive network traffic; it SHOULD change to {{enum|Dormant}} if and only if the interface is operable but is waiting for external actions before it can transmit and receive network traffic (and subsequently change to {{enum|Up}} if still operable when the expected actions have completed); it SHOULD change to {{enum|LowerLayerDown}} if and only if the interface is prevented from entering the {{enum|Up}} state because one or more of the interfaces beneath it is down; it SHOULD remain in the {{enum|Error}} state if there is an error or other fault condition detected on the interface; it SHOULD remain in the {{enum|NotPresent}} state if the interface has missing (typically hardware) components; it SHOULD change to {{enum|Unknown}} if the state of the interface can not be determined for some reason. This parameter is based on ''ifOperStatus'' from {{bibref|RFC2863}}. Because the interface includes layer 1, the {{enum|LowerLayerDown}} value SHOULD never be used.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: The textual name of the interface as assigned by the CPE.

parameters.name: Description
parameters.description: A user-friendly description of the interface.

parameters.name: LastChange
parameters.description: The accumulated time in {{units}} since the interface entered its current operational state.

parameters.name: LowerLayers
parameters.description: {{list}} {{reference|an interface object that is stacked immediately below this interface object}} See {{bibref|TR-181i2|Section 4.2.1}}. Note: Since {{object}} is a layer 1 interface, it is expected that {{param}} will not be used.

parameters.name: Upstream
parameters.description: Indicates whether the interface points towards the Internet ({{true}}) or towards End Devices ({{false}}). The upstream interface is the one that provides connectivity to the Internet or the next hop router. For example: * For an Internet Gateway Device, {{param}} will be {{true}} for all WAN interfaces and {{false}} for all LAN interfaces. * For a standalone WiFi Access Point that is connected via Ethernet to an Internet Gateway Device, {{param}} will be {{true}} for the Ethernet interface and {{false}} for the WiFi Radio interface. * For a WiFi repeater or mesh node, the interface that connects to the main router (the backhaul) is the upstream interface and {{param}} will be {{true}}. The interface that serves local devices is a downstream interface and {{param}} will be {{false}}. * For an End Device, {{param}} will be {{true}} for all interfaces that connect to the network. * For a hybrid device like a Set-Top Box (STB) that could also act as a repeater, the interface connecting to the gateway is the upstream interface ({{param}} will be {{true}}), while the interface providing the repeated signal is a downstream interface ({{param}} will be {{false}}).

parameters.name: MaxBitRate
parameters.description: The maximum upstream and downstream PHY bit rate supported by this interface (expressed in {{units}}).

parameters.name: Interface
parameters.description: The Layer 2 Ethernet Interface over which the network protocol operates, when the Type parameter is {{enum|Logical|Type}}.

parameters.name: MACAddress
parameters.description: The MAC Address of the interface. Note: This is not necessarily the same as the Ethernet header source or destination MAC address, which is associated with the IP interface and is modeled via the {{param|##.Ethernet.Link.{i}.MACAddress}} parameter.

parameters.name: LogicalNetwork
parameters.description: The textual name of the HomePlug Logical Network.

parameters.name: Version
parameters.description: Indicates the HomePlug version of the interface. This element SHOULD be in the form of dot-delimited integers, where each successive integer represents a more minor category of variation. For example: : "1.0" : "1.1"

parameters.name: FirmwareVersion
parameters.description: The firmware version of the interface.

parameters.name: ForceCCo
parameters.description: Central Coordinator (CCo) selection mode. If {{false}}, CCo selection is automatic. If {{true}}, the local HomePlug interface is forced to be CCo and all other devices in the Logical Network MUST be set to automatic CCo selection. Typically {{param}} is set to automatic CCo selection ({{false}}).

parameters.name: NetworkPassword
parameters.description: The network password of the device. This is a human readable ASCII string that is hashed per the HomePlug specification to generate the Network Membership Key (NMK). Note that care needs to be taken when setting this parameter as it might prohibit communication with other adapters or equipment connected via the powerline network.

parameters.name: OtherNetworksPresent
parameters.description: {{list}} Indicates whether any other HomePlug networks are currently visible via this interface. Examples of valid list items include, but are not limited to: : "HomePlugAV" : "HomePlug1.0" : "Other"

object.description: HomePlug interface table (a stackable interface object as described in {{bibref|TR-181i2|Section 4.2}}). Each table entry models the PHY and MAC levels of a HomePlug interface {{bibref|HPAV1.1}}.
